clue.text: Anticipate chopping all wood

indicators.note: chopping ALL cuts those letters away from the word

parts.note: to forestall = to anticipate and get in first
the letters A, L, L are cut away from the end of the word

explanation.surface: Someone expects a lumberjack to fell every tree in a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'chopping' sound like tree-felling, which suits the wood; in fact it chops the letters ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name land covered with trees, the answer usually the larger.

clue.text: Principal in favour of some turning up on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up turns SOME upside down, so it reads upwards

explanation.surface: A head teacher supports some pupils who arrive punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a vague quantity word, but it is the very letters to be turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremost means first in rank, principal.

clue.text: Lots of oil here on fancy clothes

explanation.surface: An actor slathers oil on an elaborate costume.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive rather than a synonym: a refinery is a place where lots of oil is.
explanation.definitionFit: A refinery is where crude oil is processed, so there is lots of it there.

clue.text: Love god rebuffed by Romeo becomes increasingly irritated

definitions.note: SORER is a comparative adjective: more irritated

indicators.note: rebuffed = pushed back, so the god's name goes backwards

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
Romeo is R in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Cupid, snubbed by Romeo, gets crosser and crosser.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo seems to belong with the love god in a romantic story, but he only supplies the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorer means more irritated, as in a sorer temper.

clue.text: However stock rotates, one's behind

indicators.note: rotates moves STOCK's first letter round to the end

parts.note: STOCK with its S moved to the back

explanation.surface: A trader shrugs that whichever way the shares go, somebody lags behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like the market loser trailing the pack; here it is the noun, your rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with 'behind' as the informal noun for the rear and 'one's' standing for anyone's.

clue.text: Heavy metal, you said?

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so 'you' gives the letter that sounds like it

explanation.surface: Someone checks they heard right that you are into heavy metal music.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the chemical symbol for this element, so the sound 'you' leads to its full name. 'Heavy metal' looks like the music genre.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: one of the densest metallic elements, used as nuclear fuel.

clue.text: Call them regularly and help out United

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of THEM

parts.note: first and third letters of THEM

explanation.surface: A plea to phone some people from time to time and help Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: United looks like the football club, but it gives ONE, as in people who stand united as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to call someone is to ring them up.

clue.text: Underground chamber opening in California state institution at last

indicators.note: the opening of California is its first letter
institution at last is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cave opens up beneath a California state prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'California state' reads as one phrase, but state is a verb here, AVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names a large cave, a chamber under the ground.

clue.text: They're often dressed as revolutionary youths

indicators.note: revolutionary = turning over, so AS goes backwards

explanation.surface: Young people often dress up as revolutionaries, Che Guevara T-shirts and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' suggests clothes and costumes; salads are dressed with oil and vinegar. 'As' looks like a link word but is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Salads are typically served with a dressing.

clue.text: Becomes parody, as last of employees is demoted

parts.note: final letter of employees, the S at the top of SEND UP, moved down three places

explanation.surface: A satirical sketch shows the last worker being moved to a lower post.
explanation.walkthrough: The S that starts SEND UP drops from the top of the grid entry to below END, giving END S UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up as something is to become it in the end.

clue.text: Arbitrator earned suspect votes

indicators.note: suspect = dubious, so EARNED is jumbled

explanation.surface: An adjudicator won dubious ballots, hinting at a rigged election.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural REFERENDA, not referendums, matches the plural 'votes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public votes on single questions.

clue.text: Demolish stable and flat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to raze a building to the ground
second meaning: an adjective, steady and even
third meaning: an adjective, having no slope or bumps

explanation.surface: A developer plans to knock down a stable block and a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: Stable and flat look like buildings to be knocked down, but each is an adjective: the clue is three meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for razing a building and as an adjective for even, steady ground with no slope.

clue.text: One might take ore fragment from seam in error

indicators.note: a fragment from the phrase is a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A mistaken dig pulls a chunk of ore out of the seam.
explanation.walkthrough: The mining picture hides the answer in its own words; 'fragment' sounds like a lump of rock but points to part of the text.
explanation.definitionFit: A miner is someone who extracts ore.

clue.text: Controlled ship, stuffed initially with preserved fish

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of stuffed

parts.note: kippered = cured by smoking, as herrings are

explanation.surface: A captain ran a vessel packed with smoked fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a smoked herring, and KIPPERED describes fish preserved that way.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun for a ship's captain used as a verb, in the past tense to match 'controlled'.

clue.text: Party involved in drink fiasco

indicators.note: involved in = wrapped inside

parts.note: a crew = a party, a group

explanation.surface: A group mixed up in some drunken debacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a drinks do, but it is a group of people, CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom for a botched job, from the slang verb meaning to bungle.

clue.text: With a start, he's held up inside store

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up raises HE so it reads upwards

parts.note: to rouse = to start up from sleep
HE written upwards, placed inside ROUSE

explanation.surface: A man jumps in fright after being held up at gunpoint in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a start' reads as a phrase about a fright, but it is three separate pieces: W, A and ROUSE. 'Held up' suggests a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: A warehouse is a building where goods are stored.

clue.text: Reveal 4 — low number

parts.note: to low = to moo, as cattle do

explanation.walkthrough: 4 is 4 across, BUTTOCKS: to moon is to show your bare bottom as a prank. 'Low' is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooning means baring your buttocks to someone.

clue.text: Milk supplier sure went crazy

indicators.note: crazy tells us to jumble; the fodder is SURE WENT

explanation.surface: A dairy farmer was certain and then lost his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk supplier' suggests a dairy or milkman; a wet nurse breastfeeds another woman's baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet nurse is a woman employed to breastfeed another's child.

clue.text: Two sons' 24 adhesive labels

parts.note: ticker = heart, the thing taken inside the sons

explanation.walkthrough: Read 24 across, TAKE HEART, as an instruction: S and S take a heart, TICKER, between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the self-adhesive labels children collect and put on things.

clue.text: A bird shedding hard patch

parts.note: a rhea is a large flightless South American bird
h = hard, shed from RHEA to leave REA

explanation.surface: A bird moulting leaves a bald patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shedding' suggests moulting feathers, but the bird sheds a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a patch of ground is a bounded piece of space.

clue.text: Cook starts to appreciate making a nice pasty

indicators.note: to cook the books is to rearrange them; cook jumbles the letters
the starts of appreciate and making are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of appreciate and making

explanation.surface: Instructions to bake a pasty that will be appreciated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' looks like the Cornish pastry, a pasty; here it is the adjective, pale and unhealthy-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemic means pale and sickly, pasty-faced.

clue.text: Can we hear stew cooking? It's a life-saver

indicators.note: cooking stirs STEW into new order

parts.note: can = may, as in may I?
STEW anagrammed gives WEST; WE plus ST completes it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they can hear the stew bubbling, which will save their life.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mae West is an inflatable life jacket, named after the buxom film star.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mae West life jacket saved airmen who ditched at sea.

clue.text: Monstrous dog devours a knight

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A fearsome hound gobbles up a knight in armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monstrous' seems to describe the dog but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutant can describe something monstrously altered, as in mutant creatures.

clue.text: One with purse covered in gold, returned in perfect state

indicators.note: returned sends the whole result back, reading upwards in this down clue

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a pot = a purse, a pool of prize money

explanation.surface: A rich person with a gold-covered purse comes home, which is paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: A-I-POT-U is built first, then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Thomas More's 1516 book about an ideal island commonwealth, hence any perfect state.

clue.text: Key void in piece of space-station

indicators.note: void = empty, so KEY loses its middle letter
in, read literally, means placed inside

parts.note: a slab = a piece, as of cake
KEY emptied of its inner letter

explanation.surface: Looking for a missing key part on a space station.
explanation.walkthrough: Skylab was the first US space station, launched in 1973.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one particular space-station, the first American one.

clue.text: Organise the karate rally

indicators.note: organise = arrange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to set up a martial-arts gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' looks like a noun, a meeting, but it is the verb: to recover spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to rally in spirit, to cheer up after a setback.

clue.text: First of murderers — Cain — wild and frenzied

indicators.note: first of murderers is its first letter
wild means out of control, and letters that run wild no longer keep their order, so CAIN is rearranged

explanation.surface: Cain, the first murderer in the Bible, is described as wild and frenzied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild and frenzied' reads as a pair of adjectives, but wild is the anagram instruction and only frenzied is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic means frenzied, wildly overexcited.

clue.text: Little kid picked up strength

indicators.note: picked up = heard, as by a microphone

explanation.surface: A small child was lifted by someone strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' paints a child being lifted; here it means caught by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: power and strength, as in 'with all his might'.

clue.text: Girl regularly entertained by French city's spicy dish

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of girl

parts.note: Pau is a city in south-west France

indicators.note: entertained by = hosted within

parts.note: second and fourth letters of GIRL

explanation.surface: A young woman is treated to a spicy meal by a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in city's belongs to the surface only; the definition follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is spiced rice cooked in stock, often with meat.

clue.text: Animals here include badger between outskirts of Milwaukee and Great Lake

parts.note: Lake Erie, one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Wildlife around Milwaukee and a Great Lake includes the badger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like one of the animals, but it is the verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: A menagerie is a collection of animals kept for show.

clue.text: Bee flying with 25A feeling

indicators.note: flying = scattered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: 25 across is MANIC, added to the fodder

explanation.surface: A bee buzzing about in a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies letters rather than meaning: MANIC joins BEE in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the mood or atmosphere a place gives off, the feeling in the room.

clue.text: Behead bears? Not us

indicators.note: behead cuts off the first letter

parts.note: to mother = to give birth to, as to bear does; its M is removed

explanation.surface: A gruesome command to decapitate bears, with a hasty disclaimer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' looks like the animal but is the verb, gives birth to, which in Chambers is also what 'mothers' means.
explanation.definitionFit: Defined by contrast: the people who are not us.
